editorial.description_en: A hillside at the height of the turn, seen from far enough away that the individual trees are gone.
editorial.description_ja: 紅葉した山のような、燃えるような赤茶。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.460, C 0.126, h 40.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 山 (yama, hill) + 燃え (moe, burning). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Burning Hill" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 山燃. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — sabi-iwa at ΔE00 6.7, aki-yu at ΔE00 9.1, yaki-tsuchi at ΔE00 9.9. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (220°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
